tagline.text: The central beach of Baler, the birthplace of Philippine surfing, with lodging, restaurants and surf schools close together

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–3,500 (meals, surfing and transport excluding lodging, per person per day)

airport.label: Nearest airport
airport.text: Ninoy Aquino International Airport (MNL), about 5–7 hours by road

children.text: Sabang Beach is the central beach of Baler, Aurora. It is free to enter, with surf lessons, board rentals, lodging and restaurants close by. Its gentle waves draw many beginners, and it is the signature spot of Baler, officially recognized as the birthplace of Philippine surfing.

Sabang Beach lies in Barangay Sabang in Baler, Aurora, and is the center of a Baler trip. Resorts, surf shops and restaurants line the beach, and most visitors to Baler stay here. Entrance is described as free and the beach as open 24 hours. The sand is fine and brown, turning dark brown when wet, and at midday when the waves are calm the sea looks blue.

The main attraction is the waves. Wikipedia explains that American surfer Steve Scott visited Baler in the early 1970s and that the filming of Apocalypse Now (1979 according to Wikipedia) helped establish it as a surf destination. The filming spot is called Charlie's Point. On August 6, 2023, Republic Act No. 11957 lapsed into law without the President's signature, officially recognizing Baler as the birthplace of Philippine surfing. Sabang is divided into areas such as the Outer Banks and Labasin-Sabang, and together with neighboring Cemento it is counted among the surf spots.

Reviewers say Sabang is the most accessible place for beginners. The first half of the beach has medium-sized waves that suit beginners, and larger waves are said to break toward Lindy's Point. You can surf year-round, but October–April is best, and some say the calmer summer is more stable for first-timers. Even if you do not surf, a day of walking the beach, eating dinner and resting is enjoyable enough. Cemento has whitish, grainy sand mixed with crushed coral and seashells, and is also listed as a snorkeling and diving site.

Keep in mind that fees and opening hours here come from accounts written between 2018 and 2024 and may differ today. Baler is often hit by typhoons and gets a lot of rain, so ask your lodging staff or a surf school about the weather and wave conditions first. Some sources say visitors must pay a sustainable tourism development fee of ₱100 per person, but I could not confirm this.

A board rental with an instructor is about ₱350 per hour, and a board alone is about ₱200 per hour or ₱800 per day. You can sign up directly at surf shops and resorts on the beach. On your first day, try a single hour and see how you feel.

Beginners and experienced surfers share one beach, and wave size varies from section to section, so you can choose one that suits your level. Follow your instructor's advice if you want to try the stronger sections.

blocks.title: Bayler View, a restaurant with a view

children.text: An open restaurant overlooking the beach, listed as open 6:30 AM–8:00 PM on weekdays and until 9:00 PM on Friday and Saturday. Filipino-style spaghetti and buttered chicken are recommended. Hours may change.

blocks.title: Buton Street night food and Myrtle Park

children.text: Along Buton Street, vendors sell street food such as kwek-kwek, isaw, betamax and siomai. Myrtle Park has a skatepark and is described as a hangout open from 6 PM to 1 AM.

Cemento, counted as a more challenging surf spot, is a beach in Barangay Zabali, next to Sabang. Surfers are said to prefer the morning, when the water is clearest. If you are intermediate or above, set aside a separate day.

Ermita Hill, close to town, gives a view over Baler Bay. It is described as the refuge of six families during the 1735 tidal wave. Entrance is about ₱15, and the proceeds go toward scholarships for students at a nearby college.

The San Luis Obispo de Tolosa Church was the site of the 1898–1899 Siege of Baler. The surrender on June 2 ended more than 300 years of Spanish rule, and June 30 is Philippine–Spanish Friendship Day. There are also the Quezon house and monument and the Museo de Baler. According to Wikipedia, the Museo de Baler has a mural of the 1735 tidal wave, and a branch of the National Museum opened in 2026. Check opening hours and exhibits before you visit.

blocks.title: The 600-year-old balete tree in Maria Aurora

children.text: In Balete Park, Barangay Quirino in the neighboring town of Maria Aurora, there is a balete tree about 600 years old and described as about 60 m tall. Entrance is said to be about ₱10–15, parking ₱10, and entering the hollow in its roots ₱10, and it is about 30 minutes by car from Baler town. One review mentions that some branches broke in a storm, so check the current condition locally.

items.title: Surf basics in one day
items.subtitle: A lesson and an evening on the beach

children.text: Walk the beach and look at the wave conditions. The sea is comparatively clear in the morning.
Find an instructor and a board at a surf shop near your lodging (about ₱350 per hour with an instructor).
Have a late breakfast at a beachfront restaurant and rest.
Surf once more, or rent a board only (about ₱200 per hour) and practice on your own.
Enjoy dinner and late-night snacks on Buton Street or at Myrtle Park.
Surfing takes a lot of energy. Do not overdo it on the first day, and rest if your shoulders or lower back hurt.
Arrive from Manila by bus, leave your bags at your lodging and take a walk along Sabang Beach.
Take your first lesson at a surf school, and have dinner at a local restaurant.
See Diguisit Falls and the beach on a half-day tricycle tour.
Return to town and look around Ermita Hill, the church and the museum.
Take a last surf in the morning and catch a bus back to Manila in the afternoon.
There is reportedly a 2 PM Genesis bus to Manila, so check the last bus times at the terminal.
From Cubao in Manila, Genesis buses are said to cost about ₱550 for 6–7 hours, and Joybus about ₱750 for 5–6 hours (non-stop). Some accounts give a range of ₱500–750. Fares can change.

The route to Baler crosses a mountain road, so delays are possible in rainy weather.
A tricycle to your lodging is about ₱10–20 per person. A half-day tour is about ₱300 and a full day about ₱800 (for three people).
You can rent a motorbike for about ₱800 a day or a bicycle for about ₱35 an hour.
Within Sabang Beach you can walk to most restaurants and surf shops.
Ditumabo Falls is in San Luis, about 20–45 minutes by tricycle, with an entrance fee of about ₱30, parking about ₱30 and a guide about ₱200–300. The walk takes about 20–30 minutes.
The road to Dicasalarin Cove is steep and winding, so tricycles cannot go up; a habal-habal is about ₱200–300 round trip. Entrance is about ₱300, and you register first at Costa Pacifica.
Caunayan Falls is in San Luis, with entrance of about ₱20 for adults, ₱10 for children and ₱15 for seniors.
Fees come from accounts, so reconfirm them locally.

Baler gets about 3,357 mm of rain a year, and the wettest months are December (about 454 mm), October, November and September. August and February are relatively dry. The surf season is described as October–April, when the waves are most consistent.
Beginners sometimes prefer the calmer waves of summer, so choose your season to match your goal. The average daytime high is about
and the nightly low about
, with humidity around 85%.

Lodging clusters on and around Sabang Beach. Accounts often mention The Cube by Costa, Nalu Surf Camp, Bay's Inn Resort, Endless Summer Hotel, Costa Pacifica, Playa Azul, Blue Coco Baler Beach House and Casita Baler. Baler is small, so rooms fill early on weekends, holidays and in summer.

For eating, Bayler View, Kubli Bistro in the Poblacion (4 PM–midnight, lunch about ₱250) and Dialyn's Bakeshop, known for brazo de mercedes and yema swirl, are among those mentioned. Kubli is recommended for buffalo wings and sisig a la bopes. Do not miss the local specialty Suman de Baler either. Opening hours can change.

In the evening, walk along nearby Buton Street. Buton Street is within walking distance of Sabang Beach. Check the hygiene of night-stall food yourself and drink plenty of water in the hot weather. One account notes a large coconut for about ₱20.
Early morning is when the water is clearest, according to many accounts.
Use sunscreen that is safe for coral (free of oxybenzone, benzophenone and parabens).
ATMs are scarce, so carry cash in advance.
Check the condition of your board and leash before a lesson.
Book lodging early for weekends and holidays.
Finish your day early to match the last bus time.
Do not leave trash on the beach; dispose of it properly.
On days with high waves, follow the surf school's judgment.

Between surf sessions you can walk around the Quezon house and the church in town to make the day full. It works well to split the day: sightsee in town during the hot midday, and surf in the early morning and late afternoon when the waves are good.
Waves and currents change from day to day. Surf only under the guidance of an instructor or surf school, and stay out of the water on typhoon days or when the waves are high.
Beginners should not go out into deep water alone and should surf only in the area the instructor chooses.
You can collide with boards and other surfers, so watch your surroundings.
Fees and opening hours are based on accounts from several years ago, so confirm them locally.
Baler is in the typhoon belt. Change your plans if there is a weather warning.
Do not leave your belongings on the beach unattended.
Dicasalarin Cove is a private beach that requires advance registration and is open 8:00–17:00. If you leave late, you may not get in.
The central town of Aurora, which Sabang Beach belongs to. It has a church, a museum and a market.
